Raspberry Pretzel Thumbprint Cookies

  • Isa Chandra
  • October 12, 2026
  • 2 Comments
Jump to Recipe
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:39
Instaread

These raspberry pretzel thumbprints are pillowy chocolate cookies with salty pretzel crunch, tart raspberry jam, and a drizzle of even more chocolate. The pretzel bits bake onto the exterior, so every bite gets a little salty snap against the chocolatey cookie and sweet-tart jam. It’s a journey, to be sure.

They’re playful and a little unruly and they look like a whole production, but they’re easy to make: roll the dough in crushed pretzels, press a little well into each cookie, spoon in the jam, and bake. They’re called thumbprints, but secret: it’s actually a pinkyprint. Your pinky makes the exact right size well for a teaspoon of jam. Finish with a chocolate drizzle once the cookies are cool.

Put them on a holiday cookie tray, bring them to a cookie swap, or make a batch in the middle of summer because you want them. This recipe is from I Can Cook Vegan.

Tips for The Best Chocolate Raspberry Thumbprint Cookies

Moisten your hands. The dough is stiff and a little oily, so damp hands keep it from sticking to you and help the pretzel bits grab on. Keep a little bowl of water nearby and rewet as you go.

Crush the pretzels into bits, not dust. You want little pieces of pretzel in there for crunch, so a few rolls of the pin is plenty.

Make a deep pinkyprint. Press your pinky down nice and deep so the indent holds a full teaspoon of jam. The handle end of a wooden spoon works too.

Let them cool completely. Wait until the cookies are completely cool before the chocolate goes on, or it will melt into the jam.

Raspberry Pretzel Thumbprints FAQ

Can I use a different jam? Absolutely yes. Strawberry, cherry or apricot are all lovely here, and strawberry with chocolate is never a bad idea.

Will the olive oil taste like olive oil? Nuh uh. With the cocoa, jam and chocolate going on, you won’t pick it out. But use a neutral oil like canola, avocado or sunflower if that’s what you have.

Can I make these gluten-free? I haven’t tested it, but a good 1-to-1 gluten-free baking flour and gluten-free pretzels should get you there.

How do I store them? Keep them in a loosely covered container in a cool spot for up to 4 days or so. If your kitchen runs warm, the fridge keeps the chocolate from getting soft.

Can I freeze them? For sure. Freeze them after the chocolate sets, in a single layer in an airtight container, for up to a month. Let them come to room temperature before serving.

How did I end up here? You wanted a cookie that was salty and sweet and fruity and chocolatey, and you refused to choose.

Raspberry Pretzel Thumbprint Cookies

Isa Chandra
Chocolate raspberry thumbprint cookies rolled in crushed pretzels, filled with raspberry jam and drizzled with even more chocolate. Sweet, salty and so pretty on a holiday cookie tray.
No ratings yet

Notes

~ Make sure the cookies are completely cool before drizzling the chocolate, or it will melt into the jam.
~ Moisten your hands before rolling the dough so it doesn’t stick and the pretzels adhere.
Print Recipe Pin Recipe
Prep Time 30 minutes mins
Cook Time 16 minutes mins
Additional Time (Cooling and Setting) 1 hour hr
Total Time 1 hour hr 46 minutes mins
Course Cookies, Dessert
Servings 24 cookies

Ingredients
  

  • 1/2 cup olive oil
  • 3/4 cup granulated sugar
  • 1/3 cup brown sugar
  • 1/4 cup unsweetened vegan milk
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla extract
  • 1 2/3 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
  • 3 tablespoons cornstarch
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup thin pretzel sticks
  • 3/4 cup seedless raspberry jam
  • 1/2 cup semisweet chocolate chips

Instructions
 

  • Preheat oven to 350°F. Lightly grease two large baking sheets.
  • In a large bowl beat together oil, sugar, brown sugar, milk and vanilla. Sift in flour, cocoa powder, cornstarch, baking powder and salt. Stir to form a thick, stiff dough.
  • Spread pretzels onto a large cutting board and cover with parchment paper. Roll a rolling pin over them to crush them into bits and pieces.
  • Scoop walnut-sized pieces, moisten your hands and roll into a ball. Then place them into the pretzel pieces, rolling around so that the pretzel pieces adhere. Place on prepared cookie sheets about 1 1/2 inches apart.
  • Use your pinky to make a deep indent in the center of each cookie. Use a teaspoon to fill each indent with about a teaspoon of jam. Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until the edges are firm and the bottoms are lightly browned.
  • Let cool on pan for 10 minutes or so, then place cookies on a cooling rack to cool. Wait until completely cool to proceed.
  • Place cookies on parchment or wax paper for drizzling. Using a microwave or double boiler, melt chocolate chips. Let melted chocolate cool a bit, then drizzle over cooled cookies in ribbons. Let the chocolate set in a cool room or in the fridge for 30 minutes or so.
